question.problem: Which of the following is equivalent to ${(\frac{{u}^{2}}{-2{v}^{4}})}^{5}?$
question.worked_solution:
We start by using the power of quotient rule:

$$
\begin{aligned}{(\frac{{u}^{2}}{-2{v}^{4}})}^{5} & = \\ \frac{{({u}^{2})}^{5}}{{(-2{v}^{4})}^{5}} & \end{aligned}
$$

Then, we apply the power rule in the numerator and the power of product rule in the denominator:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{{({u}^{2})}^{5}}{{(-2{v}^{4})}^{5}} & = \\ \frac{{u}^{2\cdot 5}}{(-2)^{5}\cdot {({v}^{4})}^{5}} & = \\ \frac{{u}^{10}}{(-2)^{5}\cdot {({v}^{4})}^{5}} & \end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we apply the power rule for exponents:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{{u}^{10}}{(-2)^{5}\cdot {({v}^{4})}^{5}} & = \\ \frac{{u}^{10}}{(-2)^{5}\cdot {v}^{4\cdot 5}} & = \\ \frac{{u}^{10}}{(-32)\cdot {v}^{20}} & = \\ -\frac{{u}^{10}}{32{v}^{20}} & \end{aligned}
$$
